headline: BGB and locals block BSF 'push-in' of 12 people at Kushtia border
summary: Border Guard Bangladesh and local residents thwarted an attempt by the Indian Border Security Force to push 12 individuals, including women and children, into Bangladesh.
details: Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) and local residents successfully blocked an attempt by the Indian Border Security Force (BSF) to push 12 people into Bangladesh early Friday morning.

caption:
12 people, including women and children, were nearly pushed into Bangladesh by the BSF. BGB and locals stepped in to stop it.

Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) and local residents successfully blocked an attempt by the Indian Border Security Force (BSF) to push 12 people into Bangladesh early Friday morning.

The group, which included women and children, was pushed through the Charmeghna border in the Nadia district of West Bengal, India.

Upon spotting the group, local residents intervened and, with the assistance of BGB personnel, sent the individuals back toward the area adjacent to border pillar 148.

The victims are currently stranded along the zero line of the international border.

BGB troopers and local citizens have taken up positions along the frontier to prevent any further push-in attempts by the Indian border guards.

Daulatpur Police chief Arifur Rahman stated that the BGB is directly handling the matter and legal steps will follow their directions.

headline_marked: 37 [[Bangladeshis rescued from Cambodian cyber scam compounds]] return home
headline: 37 Bangladeshis rescued from Cambodian cyber scam compounds return home
summary: The group of citizens had been trapped in scam centers in Cambodia, where they were forced to work in cybercrime operations.
details: A group of 37 Bangladeshi citizens have returned to Bangladesh after being rescued from cyber scam compounds in Cambodia.
The victims were reportedly lured to Cambodia under the guise of high-paying jobs, only to be trapped in compounds managed by cybercrime syndicates.
Once inside, they were forced to work in online scams targeting people globally, often under threat or coercion.
The rescue operation was coordinated through diplomatic channels to ensure the safe return of the victims to their home country.
This incident highlights the growing trend of human trafficking for the purpose of forced labor in cyber-scam centers across Southeast Asia.
caption:
Trapped in cybercrime compounds in Cambodia, 37 Bangladeshis have finally returned home.

A group of 37 Bangladeshi citizens have returned to Bangladesh after being rescued from cyber scam compounds in Cambodia.

The victims were reportedly lured to Cambodia under the guise of high-paying jobs, only to be trapped in compounds managed by cybercrime syndicates.

Once inside, they were forced to work in online scams targeting people globally, often under threat or coercion.

The rescue operation was coordinated through diplomatic channels to ensure the safe return of the victims to their home country.

This incident highlights the growing trend of human trafficking for the purpose of forced labor in cyber-scam centers across Southeast Asia.
